system_overview: This specification models a Byzantine Paxos consensus algorithm (BPCon), extending the PCon variant of Paxos to tolerate Byzantine (arbitrary/malicious) failures among acceptors and leaders. It abstracts and generalizes the consensus algorithm from Castro and Liskov's Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT). Good acceptors execute the Paxos protocol faithfully, while faulty acceptors may send arbitrary messages. Safety is guaranteed as long as any two Byzantine quorums share at least one good acceptor.
actors_and_components: The system has three categories of participants: (1) Good (non-faulty) acceptors that follow the protocol faithfully. (2) Fake (possibly malicious) acceptors that may send arbitrary syntactically correct messages. (3) Leaders, one per ballot, that may be faulty (any leader can send any syntactically correct message). A Byzantine quorum is a set of acceptors (real and fake) that includes a quorum of good ones. A weak quorum is a set containing at least one good acceptor.
state_variables: The system tracks four arrays indexed by good acceptor and a message set: (1) For each good acceptor, the highest ballot participated in. (2) For each good acceptor, the highest ballot in which it voted (or negative one if never voted). (3) For each good acceptor, the value voted for at the highest voting ballot (or sentinel if never voted). (4) The set of all messages ever sent. Message types include: 1a (ballot initiation), 1b (acceptor response with vote history), 1c (safety assertion), 2a (leader proposal), 2b (acceptor vote), and a special fake type that allows faulty acceptors to inject arbitrary 1b and 2b messages.
initial_state: All good acceptors have maximum ballot negative one, maximum voting ballot negative one, and sentinel voting value. No messages have been sent.
actions: Good acceptor actions mirror the non-Byzantine protocol: (1) Phase 1b: respond to a 1a message for a higher ballot with current vote state. (2) Phase 2b: vote for a value proposed in a 2a message for a ballot at least equal to the acceptor's maximum ballot. Leader actions are unrestricted since leaders may be Byzantine: (3) Phase 1a: any leader may send any 1a message at any time. (4) Phase 1c: a leader may send a 1c message for any value shown safe by a Byzantine quorum's 1b responses. (5) Phase 2a: a leader may propose any value for which a 1c message exists in the current ballot and no 2a has been sent yet. Faulty acceptor action: (6) A fake acceptor may inject any syntactically correct 1b or 2b message at any time, potentially lying about its vote history or votes.
safety_properties: An inductive invariant ensures: (1) Good acceptors maintain consistent state (maximum ballot at least equals maximum voting ballot, no votes in gaps). (2) Phase 1b messages from good acceptors accurately reflect their state. (3) Phase 1c messages correctly assert value safety (accounting for Byzantine behavior). (4) Phase 2a messages have corresponding 1c messages. (5) Good acceptors' 2b votes are consistent with their state. The key safety guarantee is that the algorithm implements the non-Byzantine PCon specification when restricted to good acceptors, which in turn implements consensus: at most one value is ever chosen.
model_bounds: Constants include the set of values, good acceptors, fake acceptors, Byzantine quorums, and weak quorums. For model checking, typical values are two values, three good acceptors, one fake acceptor, Byzantine quorums are all sets of three or more from the four total acceptors, and weak quorums are all sets of two or more. Ballots are restricted to zero through two.
additional_assumptions: Good and fake acceptor sets must be disjoint. Any two Byzantine quorums must share at least one good acceptor (the fundamental Byzantine quorum intersection property). Every weak quorum must contain at least one good acceptor. The specification uses a prophecy-constant approach: which acceptors are good versus fake is declared in advance, but good acceptors' actions do not depend on this knowledge. The ShowsSafeAt predicate for the Byzantine case requires checking that a weak quorum of 2b senders for an earlier ballot all agreed on a value, providing resilience against forged messages. The specification imports the non-Byzantine PCon module and proves refinement, with votes and maximum ballots of good acceptors serving as the refinement mapping.
